name: Deep Creek Hot Springs
access: Free, hike-in (several miles) or bike
notes: One of Southern California's best-known backcountry hot springs, on national forest land.

name: Travertine Hot Springs
access: Free, short walk from a dirt-road pullout, BLM land
notes: Multiple soaking pools with views of the Sierra Nevada, near Bridgeport.

name: Buckeye Hot Springs
access: Free, short walk, near a creek
notes: Popular free soaking spot near Travertine Hot Springs in the Eastern Sierra.

name: Strawberry Park Hot Springs
access: Paid entry, developed pools
notes: Rustic developed hot springs resort with rock-lined pools, cabins, and camping.

name: Conundrum Hot Springs
access: Free, but requires an 8.5-mile backcountry hike/permit for overnight camping
notes: A well-known but genuinely remote backcountry hot spring in the Maroon Bells-Snowmass Wilderness.

name: Fifth Water (Diamond Fork) Hot Springs
access: Free, ~2.5 mile hike, Uinta National Forest
notes: Popular waterfall-fed hot spring pools east of Spanish Fork.

name: Mystic Hot Springs
access: Paid entry, developed pools and vintage bathtubs
notes: Developed hot springs with historic claw-foot tubs and pools, plus a music venue on-site.

name: Goldbug Hot Springs
access: Free, ~2 mile steep hike, national forest land
notes: Tiered soaking pools above a canyon, one of Idaho's most-visited backcountry hot springs.

name: Burgdorf Hot Springs
access: Paid entry, historic resort
notes: Historic mining-era hot springs resort with rustic cabins, north of McCall.

name: Bagby Hot Springs
access: Paid day-use fee, ~1.5 mile hike, national forest
notes: Historic wood-flume-fed hot spring tubs in the Mt. Hood National Forest.

name: Terwilliger (Cougar) Hot Springs
access: Paid day-use fee, short hike, national forest
notes: A series of cascading soaking pools in the Willamette National Forest.

name: Umpqua Hot Springs
access: Paid day-use fee, short hike, national forest
notes: Tiered travertine pools overlooking the North Umpqua River.

name: Chena Hot Springs Resort
access: Paid entry, full resort
notes: Developed geothermal resort roughly an hour from Fairbanks, open year-round.

name: Hot Springs National Park
access: Free public fountains; paid bathhouses on Bathhouse Row
notes: The thermal springs that gave the town its name; several public jug-fountains plus historic bathhouses.

name: Ojo Caliente Mineral Springs Resort
access: Paid entry, full spa resort
notes: A developed mineral-springs resort with multiple distinct pool types (iron, arsenic, soda, lithia).

name: Spence Hot Springs
access: Free, short hike, national forest
notes: Popular natural soaking pools above the Jemez River, in the Santa Fe National Forest.

name: Boiling River
access: Free, short walk from the road, inside the park
notes: A spot where a hot spring mixes into the Gardner River near Mammoth Hot Springs — check current NPS status before visiting, it's periodically closed.

name: Granite Hot Springs
access: Paid entry, developed pool, national forest
notes: A developed soaking pool south of Jackson Hole in the Bridger-Teton National Forest.

name: Sykes Hot Springs
access: Free, but a genuinely long ~10 mile backcountry hike with permit
notes: Remote backcountry hot spring along the Big Sur coast, in the Ventana Wilderness.

name: Berkeley Springs State Park
access: Free public tap; paid historic bathhouse
notes: Historic mineral springs George Washington himself is said to have bathed in; a free public tap is on-site.
